digest.component_or_area: rebar link-audit command and dependency-link repair driver
propositions: Blocking edges written under the old ticket-type-tier rule are now wrong under the structural rule and do not self-heal, producing epics blocked by their own children and mis-escalated cross-subtree dependencies.
A new read-only store-wide scan classifies net-active blocking edges as ancestor-blocking, mis-escalated, unreadable, or clean by delegating to the shipped resolver, with an opt-in --repair.

Repair must write the replacement LINK before the stale UNLINK so a failure leaves a resumable superset rather than losing a dependency, and must fail safe on cycles, closed endpoints, and ambiguous pairs.
run_repair self-deadlocks by holding the tracker write lock across its loop while each inner write re-acquires the same non-reentrant lock, causing zero progress and a 60s flock timeout per finding.
The default invocation is read-only, takes no lock, writes nothing, and must not trigger a store reconverge (init_only=True unless --repair).

Residual mis-escalated edges whose resolved source has since closed cannot be repaired because add_dependency refuses closed-source links, but all such residuals have closed blocked sides and are inert for scheduling.
